evidence.location_or_expected_section: Implementation Changes (lines 36?37); expected complementary control in Assumptions or Public Interface specifying machine-enforceable non-compliance (e.g. refuse Apply without --allow-unverified-policy, or emit a hard fail status consumers must check)

raw_findings.failure_mechanism: Advisory-only marking does not block Apply or machine consumption, so missing-policy artifacts are silently promoted to ?compliant enough? durable outputs.
raw_findings.finding: The plan assumes a human-readable ?policy ???? mark is enough to keep missing-policy outputs from being treated as Cortex-compliant, while still allowing authoring frontmatter generation and an Apply path that can produce durable files. That assumption fails when downstream tools or users ignore advisory text and consume the file as policy-ready.
raw_findings.resolution_required: Define a hard gate: either forbid Apply when policy is missing/unverified unless an explicit override is recorded in the plan digest, or make unverified status a structured, validated field that consumers and QA must fail closed on.

evidence.location_or_expected_section: Implementation Changes (line 39) and Test Plan Plan/Apply coverage (line 46); expected Recovery / failure-mode section covering staging cleanup, crash mid-apply, orphan detection, and --accept-partial residual state

raw_findings.failure_mechanism: Process kill or partial batch Apply leaves staging debris or mixed applied/unapplied files with no defined resume, cleanup, or integrity check, violating the ?no false OKF-ready artifact? guarantee.
raw_findings.finding: The plan asserts staging before final write and that reject/failure must not leave a falsely OKF-ready target, but it never specifies recovery for crash mid-apply, orphaned staging, partial batch success under --accept-partial, or how to resume/rollback after interrupted Apply.
raw_findings.resolution_required: Specify staging lifecycle (location, uniqueness, cleanup on success/failure/crash), atomicity boundaries, --accept-partial residual reporting, and a resume/abort command or validation that detects incomplete Apply.

evidence.location_or_expected_section: Implementation Changes (line 28); expected Dependencies / Risk section covering declaration, pin, _ensure_package behavior, and failure mode when install is blocked

raw_findings.failure_mechanism: First-run or locked environments fail mid-pipeline after conversion staging, or a different YAML library silently drops comments/order, violating the preservation guarantee users rely on for Apply.
raw_findings.finding: The plan hard-requires ruamel.yaml round-trip semantics as the preservation mechanism, but nowhere handles the new runtime dependency risk (install failure, version skew vs Cortex, offline/CI environments, or fallback if ruamel is unavailable).
raw_findings.resolution_required: Declare ruamel.yaml as an explicit skill dependency with version bounds, install/ensure behavior, and a fail-closed path that never writes when round-trip preservation cannot be guaranteed.

evidence.location_or_expected_section: Assumptions (line 58) cross-cut with Public Interface prepare/apply (line 24) and --metadata-json (line 16); expected non-interactive failure/override policy

raw_findings.failure_mechanism: In headless or batch mode the Agent cannot ask, so prepare stalls, invents fields contrary to the assumption, or emits incomplete plans that Apply then blocks?without a defined exit code or required --metadata-json path.
raw_findings.finding: Semantic fields depend on Agent proposals and ?ask the user when policy basis is lacking,? but the plan provides no non-interactive recovery for CI, --plan-only automation, or batch runs where asking is impossible?while still promising deterministic prepare/publish/apply/validate subcommands.
raw_findings.resolution_required: Define non-interactive behavior: require --metadata-json for custom/required fields lacking policy basis, fail closed with a stable error, and document that Agent Q&A is optional UX only?not part of the script contract.
